name: Subchondral Insufficiency Fracture of the Knee
tags: subchondral insufficiency fracture of the knee
definition: Stress-related subchondral fracture, usually of the femoral condyle in older adults, causing acute or subacute knee pain and sometimes progressing to osteonecrosis-like collapse.

typical: Sudden or subacute medial knee pain

investigations.principle: Early radiographs can be normal; MRI is the key test for subchondral fracture and marrow edema.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Large lesions or collapse require orthopedic evaluation and may need surgery.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu/Asthi-kshaya phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Stress-related subchondral fracture, usually of the femoral condyle in older adults, causing acute or subacute knee pain and sometimes progressing to osteonecrosis-like collapse.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.

sources.title: Chronic Knee Pain / Stress Injury Imaging
